subject: Emotions
title: Carnival and Collective Joy
description: A 60-second lesson on Carnival and Collective Joy.

hook.text: Two million people dance in the streets of Rio during Carnival. Mass joy hits like a drug—because it is one.

buildup.text: Émile Durkheim called mass celebration 'collective effervescence'—a shared emotional high that bonds communities.

discovery.text: Synchronized movement—dancing, marching, chanting—releases endorphins and oxytocin simultaneously in all participants.

twist.text: Every culture has mass joy rituals: Holi, Mardi Gras, Oktoberfest. Societies that lack them report lower cohesion.

climax.text: Collective joy is political. It reminds people they belong to something larger. Governments that ban it know this.

punchline.text: Dancing together is how societies remember they are one.

quiz.question: What did Durkheim call the shared high of mass celebrations?
